analysis.session_summary: GBP led the board, closing at its best with no own releases, while AUD lagged sharply after a normal CPI miss. US Final GDP beat but produced inverted USD weakness; ADP was muted. Commodity currencies and risk proxies were mixed, with Brent up 1.087% and SPX up 0.666%. The tape shows fading of early JPY, NZD, CHF, and AUD attempts and a late USD recovery from its lows.

themes.evidence: Final GDP q/q actual 2.2% vs 1.5% forecast, polarity inverted, USD weaker 0.161%; DXY -0.182%.

themes.theme: Sterling strength without a domestic catalyst
themes.evidence: GBP rank 1, strength +0.368%, closed at its best, own releases [].
Trimmed Mean CPI miss 0.2% vs 0.3%, polarity normal, AUD weaker 0.480%; AUD rank 8 -0.328%.

currency_drivers.USD: Final GDP beat triggered inverted USD weakness; ADP muted, leaving USD only slightly lower after late recovery.
currency_drivers.EUR: No own releases; it held its range and closed modestly firmer without a clear catalyst.
currency_drivers.JPY: No own releases; attempt rejected after leading +0.41% and giving back 73%.
currency_drivers.GBP: No own releases; strongest currency, closed at its best and led the majors.
currency_drivers.AUD: Australian CPI miss drove normal AUD weakness; attempt rejected after leading +0.15% and giving back 94%.
currency_drivers.CAD: No own releases; held a weak range and was second weakest major.
currency_drivers.CHF: No own releases; attempt rejected, gave back 62% of early gains and closed near flat.
currency_drivers.NZD: No own releases; attempt rejected, gave back 87% after early lead and closed marginally firmer.

leg_notes.EUR/USD: EUR/USD built a 57.4-pip rally through the session without a clear catalyst, then gave back 35.5 pips into the close even as the GDP event moved it the other way.

polarity_reads.read: Normal polarity with AUD weakening 0.480% on a miss; positions were set for Australian inflation to confirm upside, so the miss hit AUD.
Inverted polarity with USD weakening 0.161% on a beat; market was positioned to sell dollars on any US strength, suggesting crowded USD shorts or fading good news.
Muted polarity with basket moving -0.013%; ADP did not shift USD positioning, consistent with it being a non-marginal release for the dollar tone.

scenarios.name: USD recovery extends
scenarios.thesis: Dollar recovers further from its selling rejection as FOMC speakers and US data reassert rate support, unwinding the inverted GDP reaction.
triggers: President Trump Speaks delivers pro-growth or hawkish tone
FOMC Kashkari or Waller signal more hikes
scenarios.invalidation: EUR/USD closes back above 1.13388 and pushes through the 66.9-pip daily range high.

pair_paths.rationale: Retraces today's 24.3-pip rise as USD recovers.
Cable gives back its 58.2-pip gain if USD bid returns.
Aussie remains weak after CPI miss and extends its 17.8-pip decline.

scenarios.name: GBP strength continues
scenarios.thesis: Sterling remains the strongest major, continuing to close at its best as no domestic catalyst challenges the move and risk tone stays supportive.
triggers: US data comes in soft enough to keep USD offered
scenarios.invalidation: EUR/GBP breaks back above 0.85486 and holds, signalling a sterling fade.

pair_paths.rationale: Extends its 58.2-pip daily gain as GBP outperformance persists.
Grinds through its 19.3-pip daily decline as GBP remains favored.

scenarios.name: AUD underperformance persists
scenarios.thesis: Australian CPI miss keeps AUD as weakest major, extending the 0.480% event drop and the 94% retracement of its early gain.
triggers: Risk sentiment wobbles or commodity prices fail to support AUD
scenarios.invalidation: AUD/USD closes back above 0.69508, erasing the day's weakness.

Extends its 18.7-pip daily decline as AUD is sold broadly.

risks.why_it_matters: A positive US GDP beat led to USD weakness, so further strong US data may also be sold, keeping the dollar offered.
risks.watch: ISM Manufacturing PMI, Unemployment Claims, President Trump, FOMC Kashkari/Waller.

risks.why_it_matters: AUD was the weakest major and gave back 94% of its early gain after the CPI miss, leaving it vulnerable to further downside.
risks.watch: Risk tone, Brent/USD, and any China/Australia headlines.

risks.risk: Fed speakers revive rate hike premium
risks.why_it_matters: Fed's Williams talked about one more hike; if upcoming FOMC speakers echo that, USD could recover strongly and unwind today's late bounce.
GBP closed at its best with no domestic catalyst; Bailey could challenge the move and trigger a sharp EUR/GBP rebound.
risks.watch: BOE Gov Bailey Speaks, EUR/GBP close vs 0.85486.

analysis.calendar_ahead_note: Coming window includes US ISM Manufacturing PMI, Unemployment Claims, President Trump, FOMC Kashkari/Waller, BOE Bailey, ECB Lagarde, Swiss CPI, and SNB Schlegel; these can confirm or reverse the USD recovery and GBP strength.
